title: Weather
author: @lunokjod
description: The weather of the place a person names, from the two answers OpenWeatherMap leaves at /data/weather/, in three pages. Now: the place and how old the answer is, the temperature big, and every number the service sends as a list of the system —feels like, low and high, the sky, humidity, pressure with the sea and ground levels, wind with its direction and its gusts, clouds, visibility, rain and snow, the sun, the coordinates, the country and the time of the answer. Days: each day summed up from its three-hour pieces —low, high, the sky, what it feels like, humidity, the chance of rain, the wind and its gusts, pressure, clouds, millimetres and how far one can see— so that no number is invented. Hours: every three-hour piece with everything it carries —the sky and whether it is day or night, the temperature and what it feels like, the low and the high, the wind with its direction and its gusts, humidity, pressure, clouds, the chance and the millimetres of rain or snow, and the visibility—. Every page is a `ui.list` of the system: pages, the dial, a finger and the paginator at the bottom, and the app is written in two inks, ink and paper, with the size doing the rest of the hierarchy. The sky is drawn and not only said: the icon the answer carries is painted next to the big temperature of Now and, in the day rows, at the left of each day - the eighteen icons of the service are in the app's res/ (100 x 100 with alpha, from openweathermap.org) and the file name is the icon field of the answer, so no table is needed to draw one. conditions.lua keeps the 47 weather codes the service publishes with the eighteen icons they belong to, for naming the sky with words when the answer does not. The credentials are read from /data/weather/openweather.txt (appid, lat, lon) and the gear at the top right opens a page where the key and the place are typed on the glass and saved to that same file, so a board with no credentials —or with a key the service refuses— can be fixed without a text editor. now.json and forecast.json are downloaded again only when the hour the disk keeps for them says they are older than a day —or when they are not there at all—; younger than that, the radio is not used. A memory shortage while downloading is said in the log in capitals and not mistaken for the service saying no.
